summary.text: David Osborne is a Republican state representative from Kentucky who has represented District 59 since 2005 and is seeking re-election to the Kentucky House of Representatives in the November 3, 2026 general election.
He has been Speaker of the House since January 2019.

paragraphs.text: David Osborne was born on March 27, 1964, in Oldham County, Kentucky, and received a B.S. in economics and agricultural economics from the University of Kentucky in 1986.

He worked as an auditor for the Federal Farm Credit Administration and as a realtor with H. Barry Smith Realtors, and as of May 2026 he owned and operated Deerfield Farm, which breeds thoroughbred horses for racing.
Osborne was first elected to Kentucky House District 59 in 2004.

He was the first Republican House speaker pro tempore (2017-2018), assumed the speaker's duties in 2018 after Speaker Jeffrey Hoover (R) resigned, and became speaker on January 8, 2019, which Ballotpedia describes as the longest tenure of any speaker in Kentucky history.
In the 2025-2026 session he chaired the House Committee on Committees and the House Rules Committee.
During his 2020 re-election campaign, Osborne said his priorities included "increasing workforce participation, developing infrastructure to handle growth, and alleviating inflation."
